notes: FILING-LEVEL OBSERVATION: TDG's 10-K is conspicuously program-name-silent. The defense narrative is given at the aggregate ($3,761M FY25 defense net sales, ~43% of total) without naming any Pentagon Program Element, PE number, line-item, or weapons platform of record. There are NO claims of the form 'X% of FY25 revenue came from program Y' or 'we expect FY27 deliveries under contract Z'. TDG operates as a multi-platform aftermarket components supplier (90% proprietary, no customer >10%), so the J-Book DIVERGENCE PATTERN that this cohort tests for (forward narrative load-bearing on a named PE that is shrinking/unfunded) is structurally inapplicable here. This is itself a discriminative finding: the divergence pattern requires program-specific narrative load, which TDG does not provide.
